Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Fix bugs and troubleshoot issues reported by users or QA
Situation2: A minor UI glitch occasionally shows up but has an easy workaround
Story: My phone buzzed violently on the nightstand, jolting me awake. It was 2:13 a.m. I squinted at the screen—my best friend’s name glowed in the darkness. I answered, and immediately heard sobs. Through broken words, she told me her father had just been rushed to the hospital. She needed me to listen, to be there, to help her hold together the pieces. I sat up, heart pounding, trying to offer comfort, but my mind kept drifting. Just before bed, I’d seen a Slack message from QA about that annoying UI glitch. It wasn’t critical, but the product manager wanted it fixed before tomorrow’s demo. I knew I could patch it in half an hour, but if I left my friend now, she’d feel abandoned. If I ignored the bug, I’d let my team down. My friend’s voice trembled in my ear, and I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in, each demanding something I wasn’t sure I could give.
